hook.line: When Vale asks who went to the neighbourhood assembly, Tomás needs two verbs. *Asistir* means to be there, and it does not mean "assist".
hook.es: Yesid no asistió a la asamblea.
hook.en: Yesid did not attend the assembly.

examples.en: More than a hundred people attended.

examples.es: Faltó a la reunión sin avisar.
examples.en: She missed the meeting without telling anyone.

examples.es: Asistí a la boda de mi prima.
Yesid no asistió a la asamblea.
examples.en: Yesid did not attend the assembly.
The attendees applauded at the end.

rule:
*Asistir a* means to attend an event: *asistí a la boda*. It is not "assist": for helping, Spanish says *ayudar*.

*Faltar a* means to miss something you were expected at: *faltó a la reunión*. Count the misses before *a*: *faltó tres veces a clase*.

Both need *a* before the event. People who attend are *los asistentes*.

In the news, *asistieron* with a number is the standard way to give a crowd size.
smallPrint: Teachers call *asistir* and *faltar* verbs of attendance. Both take *a*, like *ir a*.

options: More than a hundred people helped.

More than a hundred people were missing.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *asistí* or *asistió*: ___ a la boda de mi prima. (I was there.) Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Asistí a la boda de mi prima.
yourTurn.why: *Asistí* is "I attended"; *asistió* is "he or she attended".

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *a* or *de*: Faltó ___ la reunión sin avisar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Faltó a la reunión sin avisar.
yourTurn.why: Both *faltar* and *asistir* take *a* before the event.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: More than a hundred people attended.
Type in Spanish: She missed class three times.
yourTurn.why: *Faltar a* plus the number of times.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Asistí a la boda.*
Say it about us: *Faltó a la reunión.*
Type in Spanish, to a friend: Did you attend the vote?
yourTurn.why: *Asististe* is the "you" form for the past.

pitfalls.wrong: Asistí la boda de mi prima.
pitfalls.right: Asistí a la boda de mi prima.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Asistir* always takes *a* before the event.

pitfalls.wrong: Asistí a mi prima con la boda.
pitfalls.right: Ayudé a mi prima con la boda.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Asistir* means to attend; to help someone, Spanish says *ayudar*.

pitfalls.right: Faltó a la reunión sin avisar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. To miss an event, *faltar* needs *a*.

personal: Say which event you attended last, and one you missed: *Asistí a… y falté a…*
